mainTopic: The order of the יום הכיפורים service: the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה, the leftover blood (שירים), and רבי חנינא's ruling on scooping the incense
overview: The ברייתא records a dispute about which parts of the כהן גדול's white-garment service on יום הכיפורים must stay in order. According to רבי יהודה, only the inside service must stay in order. According to רבי נחמיה, all the white-garment actions must stay in order. The גמרא first explains each view through the words 'once a year.' It then rejects that explanation for רבי יהודה and derives both views from two limiting words, 'זאת' and 'אחת.' For רבי נחמיה, one of those words teaches that the leftover blood (שירים) is not essential. For רבי יהודה, the שירים follow the other outside actions. A ברייתא then brings a dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה about 'וכלה מכפר.' רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue over what practical difference that dispute makes. A view attributed to רבי יוחנן clashes with his own statement in זבחים, and the גמרא leaves it as a קשיא. Finally, רבי חנינא rules that incense scooped before the bull was slaughtered does not count. The גמרא asks whether this can fit רבי יהודה and raises a challenge from the משנה about spilled blood, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two readings of 'once a year'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads 'once a year' as a place. רבי נחמיה reads it as all the actions of the day's כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that 'once a year' means the place where atonement happens once a year. רבי נחמיה holds that it means the things through which atonement happens once a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה disagree. Each one reads the verse's phrase 'once a year' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'once a year' points to a place, the קודש הקדשים. So only the actions done there must stay in order. For רבי נחמיה, it points to all the actions of the day done in white garments, so even the white-garment actions outside must stay in order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
a place in which atonement is achieved
once a year.
And Rabbi Nechemya holds:
things through which atonement is achieved
phrases.notes: All the white-garment actions, inside and outside.

phrases.english: once a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute in the ברייתא that came on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: only the actions in the place of yearly atonement (inside) must stay in order. רבי נחמיה: all the actions of yearly atonement (all white-garment service) must stay in order.

steps.title: The verse never says 'place'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה's reading. The verse does not mention a place at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the verse write the word 'place' according to רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave for רבי יהודה. The words 'once a year' say nothing about a location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Once a year' sounds like it describes the whole day's service, not one room. So it is hard to say that רבי יהודה drew a limit about place from these words. This challenge sets up a new explanation of his source.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (introduces a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Is that to say that according to Rabbi Yehuda 'place' is written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's half of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה reads 'once a year' as referring to a place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse contains no word meaning 'place,' so a limit based on location cannot come from it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's real source: two limiting words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the 'place' explanation. רבי יהודה actually learns from two limiting words, 'זאת' and 'אחת.' Each one excludes a group of actions from the requirement of order.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי יהודה's reason: it is written 'this,' and it is written 'once.' One word excludes the white-garment actions done outside, and the other excludes the gold-garment actions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation for רבי יהודה. Two words in the פסוק each narrow the rule of order, and together they leave only the inside service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' means the earlier explanation is dropped. 'זאת' and 'אחת' are both limiting words. One removes the white-garment actions done outside from the rule, and the other removes the gold-garment actions. What remains under the rule is only the white-garment service inside.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both sides of the dispute will now be built on the same two words. Their disagreement becomes a question of what the second exclusion is used for.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda:
It is written 'this,' and it is written 'once.'
phrases.notes: Both are limiting words in ויקרא ט״ז:ל״ד.

phrases.english: one is to exclude white garments outside,
and one is to exclude gold garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 by replacing the explanation entirely.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and replacement: a new derivation from the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה reads 'once a year' as a place.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה learns from two limiting words: one excludes the white-garment actions outside, and one excludes the gold-garment actions.

steps.title: How רבי נחמיה uses the two words
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה uses one word to exclude the gold-garment actions. He uses the other to teach that the leftover blood (שירים) is not essential to the order.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נחמיה? One word excludes the gold garments, and one excludes the leftover blood, which is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unstated question: what does רבי נחמיה do with these two limiting words? He uses the second word for a different exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה holds that all the white-garment actions outside must stay in order. So he cannot use a word to exclude them. Instead, he uses the second word to exclude pouring the שירים: even though it is a white-garment action done outside, doing it out of order does not invalidate the service.

keyTerms.meaning: leftover blood, poured at the base of the מזבח
are essential / invalidate if missing or out of order

phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya?
phrases.notes: An implied question: how does he use the two words?

phrases.english: one is to exclude gold garments,
and one is to exclude the leftover blood, that it is not essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two-word source to רבי נחמיה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One word excludes the gold-garment actions, and the other excludes the שירים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה on the leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, the שירים follow the same rule as the other outside actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? If they are essential, they are essential. If they are not essential, they are not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה needs no special word to exclude the שירים. For him, they simply share the status of the other outside actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already excluded all the white-garment actions outside, and pouring the שירים is one of them. The שירים have no separate status: whatever applies to the outside actions applies to them too. The next step brings a ברייתא to support this.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
if they are essential, they are essential,
and if they are not essential, they are not essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts רבי יהודה with רבי נחמיה's special exclusion of the שירים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה holds about the שירים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שירים share the status of the other outside actions and need no separate exclusion.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a doubt or an 'I don't know.' It means the שירים have no special status of their own and are treated like the rest of the outside service.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי עקיבא's reading of 'and he finished atoning'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is cited. רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as saying that once atonement is achieved, the service is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And he finished atoning for the קודש.' If he atoned, he finished. If he did not atone, he did not finish. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support what it said about רבי יהודה. This part gives רבי עקיבא's opinion first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns from 'וכלה מכפר' that achieving atonement is what counts as finishing. Once the blood that brings atonement has been sprinkled, the service is complete, even if something like pouring the שירים is still left.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'And he finished atoning for the sacred place'
if he atoned, he finished,
and if he did not atone, he did not finish,
the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a ברייתא to support Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view on the שירים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה on 'וכלה מכפר את הקודש.'

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reading: every sprinkling is required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reverses רבי עקיבא's reading. Only finishing brings atonement, so missing even one sprinkling means nothing was accomplished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Why not say, if he finished, he atoned, and if he did not finish, he did not atone? This teaches that if he left out even one of the sprinklings, he has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה offers the opposite reading. It is the completion of every sprinkling that brings the כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reading means that atonement equals completion. רבי יהודה's reading means that completion is required before there is any atonement. Under his view, leaving out a single מתנה cancels the whole thing. The גמרא will explain next how this dispute connects to the שירים.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה excludes the outside white-garment actions from the requirement of order, and he treats the שירים like them. רבי נחמיה requires order for all white-garment actions except the שירים. In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה holds that every single מתנה is essential for the כפרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
Why should we not say:
if he finished, he atoned,
and if he did not finish, he did not atone,
so that if he left out one of the sprinklings
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with רבי יהודה's counter-reading of רבי עקיבא's interpretation.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view of what is essential to the כפרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the ברייתא that missing one מתנה invalidates everything.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked about this: what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה changes anything in practice. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings seem to lead to the same result: the כפרה is not complete until every sprinkling (מתנה) has been done. So the גמרא wants to know whether רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה argue only about how to read 'וכלה מכפר,' or whether there is a real difference in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And we said (about this). It introduces a discussion recorded elsewhere.
What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: And we said: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what difference the argument in Steps 6 to 7 makes in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה differ in practical halacha or only in how they read the פסוק.

steps.title: Two אמוראים give two answers
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says they argue only about how to read the פסוק. The other says they argue about whether the שירים are essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagreed. One said the difference is only in how they read the פסוק. The other said the difference is whether the leftover blood is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in two ways. One sees no practical difference. The other sees a real difference about the שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first view, both sides reach the same halacha and only read the words differently. According to the second view, רבי יהודה ("only finishing brings atonement") holds that the שירים are essential. רבי עקיבא ("once atonement is achieved, the service is finished") holds that they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: The way they read the verse. This means a difference in reading only, not in practical law.
The leftover blood poured at the base of the מזבח after the sprinklings
Are essential. Without them, the service does not work.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say here which אמורא said which view. The next step's challenge is directed at a position attributed to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi (disagreed).

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: One said: The difference between them is only in how they read the verse.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: שִׁירַיִם מְעַכְּבִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: And one said: The difference between them is whether the leftover blood is essential.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either there is no practical difference (only a difference in reading), or the difference is whether the שירים are essential.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Elsewhere רבי יוחנן said that רבי נחמיה holds the שירים are essential. That clashes with what is assigned to him here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? Didn't רבי יוחנן say that רבי נחמיה taught like the one who holds the leftover blood is essential?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view assigned to רבי יוחנן. It does this by quoting a different statement of רבי יוחנן (in זבחים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation of רבי נחמיה's view (Step 4) says that in his opinion the שירים are not essential, and this is attributed to רבי יוחנן. But in זבחים, רבי יוחנן said that רבי נחמיה taught like the one who holds the שירים ARE essential. The same אמורא cannot hold both views about רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? This opens a challenge.
But didn't he say...? This brings a contradicting statement.
Taught (here: he held this view in his teaching)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Rabbi Nechemya taught
in line with the one who says the leftover blood is essential!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges, from רבי יוחנן's own statement in זבחים, the view attributed to him that רבי נחמיה holds the שירים are not essential (Step 4).
steps.kashyaTarget: The attribution to רבי יוחנן of the view that, according to רבי נחמיה, the שירים are not essential (Step 4).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבי יוחנן says רבי נחמיה holds the שירים are essential, which contradicts this.

steps.title: The contradiction is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the contradiction stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the challenge. It simply says the question remains a difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "קשיא" alone means there is no answer. The contradiction in רבי יוחנן's words stays open, but the discussion moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question stays unanswered.

steps.whatToRemember: The question "what is the practical difference" got two answers. The answer assigned to רבי יוחנן (about the שירים) clashes with his statement in זבחים, and this is left as an unresolved קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 10 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction in רבי יוחנן's statements is not resolved.

steps.title: Incense scooped before the bull was slaughtered is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that if the כהן גדול scooped the incense before slaughtering his bull, the scooping does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: If the כהן גדול scooped the incense before the bull was slaughtered, he did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי חנינא teaches that the order between slaughtering the bull and scooping the incense is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is: first slaughter the bull, then scoop the incense. רבי חנינא says that breaking this order cancels the scooping completely, so it must be done again.

keyTerms.meaning: He scooped it with his hands
He did nothing at all. The action does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: קְטוֹרֶת שֶׁחֲפָנָהּ קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָתוֹ שֶׁל פַּר —
phrases.english: Incense that he scooped before the slaughter of the bull —
he did nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic related to the order of the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scooping the incense before the bull is slaughtered is invalid. The order here is essential.

steps.title: This cannot follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רבי חנינא follows and argues it cannot be רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Not רבי יהודה's. Because רבי יהודה said that the word "חוקה" (which makes the order essential) only refers to the actions done inside in white garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify whose opinion רבי חנינא follows. It concludes that it cannot be רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, only the inside actions in white garments must be in order. Scooping the incense happens outside, so for him its order should not matter. Yet רבי חנינא makes it essential.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion is this?
"Statute." The word that makes the order essential.
The white garments of the כהן גדול on יום כיפור

phrases.english: Like whom? Not like Rabbi Yehuda,
for if it were Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say:
when "statute" is written —
it is about actions done in white garments
inside that it is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose opinion רבי חנינא's ruling follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion רבי חנינא's ruling follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי יהודה, because he limits the requirement of order to inside actions.

steps.title: Outside actions for the inside count as inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה could agree, because scooping for the inside service counts as an inside action.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה: something done for the needs of the inside is treated like the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that רבי חנינא cannot follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The incense is scooped outside, but it is scooped only to be brought into the קודש הקדשים. So רבי יהודה could treat the scooping like an inside action, and the order would then be essential.

keyTerms.meaning: An action done for the needs of the inside service
It is treated like the inside

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Yehuda;
what is done for the needs of the inside is like the inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 13's conclusion that רבי חנינא cannot follow רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי חנינא's ruling contradicts רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed scooping counts as an outside action. But scooping for the inside service may count as inside.

steps.title: The משנה about spilled blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if blood spills, he brings new blood and sprinkles again, without mentioning new incense. This suggests the scooping does not count as inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If the blood spilled before he finished the inside sprinklings, he brings other blood and sprinkles again inside from the beginning. If outside actions done for the inside counted as inside, the משנה should have said he must scoop the incense again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea of Step 14 using a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the blood spills, a new animal is slaughtered. Now the incense was scooped before this new slaughter, so the order is broken. If scooping counted as an inside action, he would need to scoop again. The משנה does not require this, which shows that the order of the scooping is not essential.
steps.confusionAlert: The point is not about the spilled blood itself. It is about what the משנה leaves out: it never says to scoop new incense, even though the old scooping now comes before the new slaughter.

phrases.english: We learned: If, before he finished
the inside sprinklings, the blood spilled —
he brings other blood,
and sprinkles again from the beginning inside.
And if it were so (that it counts as inside),
it should have said he must scoop again!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָּמַר מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבִּפְנִים נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the idea of Step 14 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that scooping for the inside service counts as an inside action.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the new slaughter, the earlier scooping is out of order. Yet the משנה does not require scooping again, so the scooping must not count as an inside action.
